newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Nigeria protests minister's delay at N.Y. airport.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria protests minister's delay at N.Y. airport.

text.p: Nigeria has complained that its Foreign Minister, Tom Ikimi, was humiliated by being delayed by immigration authorities at New York's John F. Kennedy airport after arriving September 26 to attend the U.N. General Assembly.

In a letter to the U.S. mission to the United Nations published on Tuesday, Nigerian U.N. envoy Ibrahim Gambari said Ikimi was told immigration officials were trying to get State Department clearance "following their observation that the visa issued to the minister and his entourage had restrictions on their movements while in the United States."

Nigerian diplomats are restricted from travelling outside a 25-mile (40-km) radius of New York and Washington as part of U.S. sanctions prompted by alleged human rights abuses and lack of democracy in Nigeria.

Gambari said Ikimi was aware of the restrictions before leaving Nigeria and had visited the United States several times before, subject to the same restrictions but without experiencing delays at the airport.

"The (Nigerian) Mission has therefore concluded that what happened at the airport...was a deliberate attempt to embarrass and humiliate the Foreign Minister of the Federal Republic of Nigeria," he said.
"The Mission protests in strong terms against this unwarranted incident and requests that it be promptly clarified so as to avoid any repetition of same in the future."
